challenges.name: recovery-rebuild-leaderboard
challenges.title: Recovery: rebuilding the leaderboard while learners keep writing
challenges.description: Two rebuild runs of the CodeDev leaderboard after Redis came back empty. Read the runbook output and the metrics, then decide whether each statement is true.

questions.question:
Rebuild drill in staging (first version of the new job), Tuesday:

14:20:00 redis-lb flushed for the drill
14:20:05 rebuild start: watermark W = max(seq) of progress_event = 9,874,102
14:20:05 building lb:v8:* in batches of 5,000 events (seq 1..W)
14:23:16 batch 1975/1975 done, cursor = 9,874,102
14:23:16 SET lb:current v8   -> readers switched
-- meanwhile the leaderboard consumer kept running and applied each new event to lb:current, which still pointed at v7 (the flushed keys) until 14:23:16
-- progress_event rows with seq > W at 14:23:16: 5,318 (load test traffic)

Statement: "Once lb:current points at v8, the boards are complete: every progress event written before the switch is counted in them."
questions.explanation: False. The rebuild stopped at the watermark W it read at 14:20:05. The 5,318 events written during the 3 minutes 11 seconds of the rebuild have seq > W, so the rebuild never read them, and the consumer applied them to v7, which nobody reads after the switch. Those learners lost points on the board even though PostgreSQL has every event. The fix is the catch-up phase: after reaching W, keep reading the log from the cursor until it reaches the current head, switch only then, and let the live consumer continue from the last seq the rebuild applied (skipping any seq at or below it). The misconception is that the watermark is where the rebuild ends; it is only where the bulk copy ends.

questions.question:
A later loss of Redis, rebuilt with the new job, 40% through the bulk copy. Two ways to answer GET /leaderboard?board=alltime&n=3 during the rebuild:

(a) from the keys being built, lb:v9:alltime:
    1. u_2203  7,410   2. u_0815  7,050   3. u_1290  6,980
(b) from the hourly snapshot (asOfSeq 9,790,118, taken 41 minutes before Redis was lost), with status "rebuilding":
    1. u_0815 18,920   2. u_2203 18,450   3. u_4471 17,990

Metrics during the rebuild: progress writes p95 45 ms (same as before), PostgreSQL CPU 38%, each batch 5,000 events in about 95 ms.

Statement: "Answering from (b) with a 'rebuilding' status is the better choice: (a) shows each learner only the events read so far, so ranks and points look like learners lost most of their progress."
questions.explanation: True. Keys under construction contain only the first 40% of the log, so every score in (a) is too low and the order is wrong (u_4471 is missing from the top 3 because most of their events are not read yet). A snapshot is stale but internally consistent, and the status lets the web app say "Leaderboard is being refreshed" instead of showing wrong numbers. That is why the switch happens only when the new keys are complete, with one write (the lb:current pointer), so readers move from the snapshot to the full board at once. The misconception is that the freshest data is always the best answer: a partial projection is fresh but wrong, which is worse than a labelled, 41-minute-old snapshot.

challenges.name: recovery-rebuild-leaderboard
challenges.title: Recovery: rebuild the leaderboard after losing Redis
challenges.description:
Redis came back empty and with it the CodeDev leaderboard: the sorted sets for "alltime" and for each week ("weekly:2026-W44"). The progress events in PostgreSQL (an append-only log, seq 1, 2, 3, ...) are the source of truth. Write LeaderboardService so that it rebuilds both kinds of board from the log in batches, without blocking writes, serves the last known top N from an hourly snapshot while rebuilding, catches up the events written during the rebuild, and switches readers to the new boards at once.

Methods (the runner calls them; the interfaces are in the file):
- startRebuild(): Redis was lost (it may happen again, even in the middle of a rebuild): go back to "rebuilding", forget any partial rebuild and start again from the first event of the log, writing into new keys.
- step(): one background batch, only while rebuilding: one call log.read(cursor, batchSize) (events with seq > cursor, at most batchSize), add each event's points to the learner in "alltime" and in "weekly:<event.week>" of the new keys (cache.zincrby), move the cursor to the last seq read. If after that the cursor is >= log.headSeq() (the head moves while learners keep writing), switch: readers use the new keys from now on, status "ready", and the last applied seq is the cursor. A step with an empty batch at the head also switches.
- onEvent(event): a new event was appended to the log. While rebuilding, do nothing (the rebuild reads it from the log). When ready, add it to the live boards unless its seq is <= the last applied seq (the bus delivers at least once), then remember its seq.
- read(board, n): board must match "alltime" or "weekly:<4 digits>-W<2 digits>", else { status: "error", error: "unknown_board" }; then n must be an integer from 1 to 100, else { status: "error", error: "invalid_limit" }. Ready: { status: "ready", top: cache.ztop(liveKey, n) }. Rebuilding: { status: "rebuilding", asOfSeq: snapshot.asOfSeq, top: the first n entries of snapshot.boards[board], or [] if the snapshot has no such board }.
top entries are [userId, score], highest first, ties by userId (cache.ztop sorts that way; a missing key gives []).

Input: { batchSize, snapshot: { asOfSeq, boards }, log: [{ userId, week, points }] (seq 1..), script }. The runner creates the service on an empty Redis and calls startRebuild(). Steps: { tick: k } calls step() k times; { write: { userId, week, points } } appends an event to the log, then calls onEvent; { redeliver: seq } calls onEvent again with that logged event; { read: board, n } records read(board, n); { flush: true } empties Redis, then calls startRebuild(). After the script the runner calls step() until "alltime" reads "ready".
Output (JSON): reads (each with its board and n) and final (the top 100 of "alltime" and of every week in the log).
hints: Draw the log as a line with three marks: where the rebuild cursor is, where the head was when the rebuild started, and where the head is now. Which events would be missing if you switched when the cursor reached the second mark, and who else could add them?

The state lives in a few fields: the status, the version of the keys being built, the version readers use, the cursor and the last applied seq. Check which of them startRebuild must reset, which one step() changes for the switch, and what read() looks at to choose between the snapshot and the live keys.

A similar rebuild for a search index: build into catalog_v12 from the courses table in pages of 500 ids, keep paging until the last id read equals the current max id (new courses keep arriving), then repoint the alias "catalog" from v11 to v12 in one call; the change feed then applies only changes with an id above the last one indexed, and search answers from the cached top results with a "refreshing" flag until the alias moves.

tests.name: Batch of 3: reads serve the snapshot while rebuilding, then the rebuilt boards
Writes during the rebuild are caught up from the log before the switch
After the switch, live writes are applied once and a redelivered event is skipped
Redis is lost again in the middle of the rebuild: start over from the first event
Lost again after it was ready: back to the snapshot until the new rebuild switches
Edge cases: empty log, a week the snapshot lacks, a week with no events
Invalid reads: unknown board names and limits outside 1..100
Large input: 1,200 events, 300 learners, batch 100, writes, redeliveries and a second loss
